card.name: Limits and thresholds after 'up to'
card.fires_on: Words in a clause that follows a stated upper limit or maximum, where the text goes on to say what happens beyond that point. Examples are 'at which time', 'there is' and 'before'.

modes.label: Beyond-the-limit clause
modes.description: Linking words right after a stated maximum, leading into what happens past it.
modes.example: late up to ten working days at which<< time>> a mark of zero

modes.label: Limited experience at high doses
modes.description: 'there is' after a higher dose range, introducing little or no experience with it.
modes.example: are not needed and there<< is>> no controlled experience with such doses

modes.label: Limit on an effect
modes.description: Words stating there is a limit to how far something can be increased.
modes.example: can be increased<< before>> the aperture is so small that light dif

card.writes: It promotes words such as 'eventually', 'beyond' and 'diminishing', which suggests it prepares text about what happens past a limit.
card.plain: It fires after a stated maximum, when the text is about to say what happens past that point.
